I have everything needed. Here are my findings.

## Summary

**No Redis anywhere in this repository.** This is the `usememos/memos` project (Go backend + React/TypeScript frontend). Caching is a hand-rolled **in-memory** cache. The "user" cache uses the default TTL of **10 minutes**.

## 1. Redis usage — NONE

- No `redis`, `ioredis`, or `node-redis` in Go deps (`/bench/repo/go.mod`, `/bench/repo/go.sum`) or JS deps (`/bench/repo/web/package.json`, `/bench/repo/web/pnpm-lock.yaml`).
- No `docker-compose` file, no `.env` files, no Redis connection strings.
- The only `createClient` hits are false positives — they are ConnectRPC (`@connectrpc/connect`) RPC clients in `/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts` (lines 2, 72, 192-203), unrelated to Redis.
- The grep hits for "redis" were substring matches inside those `createClient`/interceptor lines, not Redis.

## 2. Cache layer — in-memory, custom implementation

Backed by a thread-safe in-process cache (Go `sync.Map`), not Redis or any external store.

- Implementation: `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`
  - `Cache` struct backed by `sync.Map` (line 67-73).
  - Per-item expiration timestamps (`item.expiration`, line 37); lazy eviction on `Get` (lines 135-144) plus a background `cleanupLoop` goroutine (lines 199-215) running on `CleanupInterval`.
  - `MaxItems` cap with oldest-item eviction (`cleanupOldest`, lines 253-313).
- Wired up in `/bench/repo/store/store.go`:
  - Three caches: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (lines 27-29), all created via `cache.New(cacheConfig)` (lines 51-53).
  - Closed/cleaned up on shutdown (lines 74-76).

## 3. TTL for "user" cache entries — 10 minutes (the default TTL)

- The user cache is populated exclusively via `s.userCache.Set(...)`, which applies the **default TTL** (no `SetWithTTL` override for users):
  - `/bench/repo/store/user.go` lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167 — all `Set` calls.
  - `Get` at `/bench/repo/store/user.go` lines 150-151; cache key builder `userCacheKey` at lines 88-96.
  - User cache invalidation: `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go` line 40 (`deleteUserCache` → `userCache.Delete`).
- `Set` delegates to `SetWithTTL(..., c.config.DefaultTTL)` — `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` lines 93-95.
- The `DefaultTTL` value is **10 minutes**, set in two places:
  - `/bench/repo/store/store.go` line 41: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` (this is the config actually used for `userCache`).
  - `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` line 59: `DefaultConfig()` also `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` (default helper, not the one wired into the store).

So: user cache entries expire **10 minutes** after being set. There is no user-specific/custom TTL — it inherits the store-wide default. Related config also sets `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` and `MaxItems: 1000` (`/bench/repo/store/store.go` lines 42-43).

Note: unrelated "expire"/"cache" hits exist elsewhere and are not part of this cache layer — S3 object expiry (`/bench/repo/internal/storage/s3/s3.go:79`), memo-share expiry (`/bench/repo/store/memo_share.go:12`), and on-disk attachment thumbnail/motion cache folders (`/bench/repo/store/attachment.go:75-76`).
